steps.do: Confirm the Playwright config file exists at the project root.
Run the locale spec in headless Chromium.
Run only the tests whose names contain locale.
Confirm the HTML report folder was written.

K-019002.check: Playwright prints '2 passed' with no failures and exits 0.

steps.do: Confirm @axe-core/playwright is listed in devDependencies.

traps: Scanning only English misses German labels that overflow and fail contrast.

steps.do: Confirm App.vue sets the dir attribute from the active locale.

steps.do: Create the component folder for the modal.
Create Modal.tsx that renders its children through createPortal from react-dom into document.body.
Add a useEffect that listens for keydown and calls onClose when event.key equals Escape, returning a cleanup function that removes the listener.
Return null from Modal when the open prop is false so nothing mounts.
Type-check the new file with the TypeScript compiler.

K-019006.example: Modal.tsx exports Modal with props open (boolean), onClose (function), and children (ReactNode), and calls createPortal(content, document.body) when open is true. Pressing Escape while open calls onClose exactly once.
K-019006.check: npx tsc --noEmit prints nothing and exits 0, and a Vitest test that fires a keydown Escape event expects onClose toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1).
traps: Small models often forget the cleanup function, so the keydown listener stacks up on every open.
Do not use ReactDOM.render, which was removed in React 19; use createRoot or createPortal.
Do not read document.body during server rendering without a typeof document check.

steps.do: Create Dialog.tsx with a useRef typed as HTMLDialogElement, and a useEffect that calls showModal when open becomes true and close when it becomes false.
Listen to the dialog close event and call the onClose prop so Escape keeps React state in sync.
Install dialog-polyfill for test browsers that lack showModal.
Run the type checker to confirm the ref type matches the dialog element.

K-019007.example: Dialog.tsx calls dialogRef.current.showModal() in a useEffect when open becomes true, and its close event handler calls onClose. Browsers without showModal load the dialog-polyfill import.
K-019007.check: npx tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no output, and npm ls dialog-polyfill prints a line containing dialog-polyfill@ followed by a version number.
traps: Calling showModal on an already open dialog throws InvalidStateError, so check dialog.open first.
Do not set position fixed on the dialog itself, because the browser top layer already positions it.
React 19 accepts ref as a plain prop, so forwardRef is not needed.

Return false from getServerSnapshot so server rendering never touches window.
Write a Vitest test that mocks matchMedia with matches true and asserts the hook returns true.

Remove the listener in the unsubscribe function returned from subscribe, or it leaks.
Use the same query string in CSS and JavaScript so the breakpoints match.
